questions.q: Where is a Unity Catalog metastore created and managed?
options: Only through a support ticket to Databricks
By any user inside any workspace's settings page
Automatically, with no admin action required
By account admins in the account console, not inside a single workspace
questions.explain: Metastores are created and managed at the account level by account admins, since a metastore's purpose is to span workspaces rather than belong to one.

questions.q: What is Databricks' rule for how many metastores exist per region?
options: One Unity Catalog metastore per region, per account
Exactly one metastore for the entire account regardless of region
One metastore per catalog
One metastore per workspace
questions.explain: Databricks provisions one metastore per region per account; workspaces in the same region typically attach to that same regional metastore.

questions.q: How many metastores can a single workspace be assigned to at one time?
options: Exactly two, for redundancy
Exactly one
Zero, workspaces never attach to metastores
Unlimited
questions.explain: A workspace attaches to exactly one metastore at a time, while a metastore can have many workspaces assigned to it — a many-to-one relationship.

questions.q: What does a metastore actually store?
options: Nothing; it is purely a routing address with no stored state
Only user passwords and login credentials
A full copy of every table's data, independent of cloud storage
Metadata — catalog/schema/table definitions and permissions — plus (optionally) a managed storage location, not your actual table rows
questions.explain: A metastore stores metadata and governance information; actual managed-table data lives in cloud object storage that the metastore tracks, not inside the metastore itself.

questions.q: Which SQL statement returns the metastore the current session is attached to?
options: DESCRIBE METASTORE CURRENT;
GET CURRENT_METASTORE();
SELECT CURRENT_METASTORE();
SHOW METASTORE STATUS;
questions.explain: SELECT CURRENT_METASTORE(); is the real Databricks SQL function that returns the ID of the currently attached metastore.
